matches.rationale: Both identify the same issue: the abstract claims FID scores (2.38–2.64 in GT, 2.15–2.38 in findings) that are cherry-picked or unsupported by Table 4, which shows worse performance at higher replacement ratios. The core scientific issue—selective reporting of favorable results in the abstract—is identical.

GT describes ambiguity in Equation 2's regression objective definition and the role of conditioning variable c in activation distillation. No finding addresses this methodological inconsistency in the loss function formulation.

GT identifies missing hyperparameter details in Table C.1 (gradient clipping specification, warmup schedule details, batch size clarification). No finding addresses these experimental protocol omissions.

Both identify overstated claims about grafting's generality. GT notes the introduction's absolute language ('proves,' 'demonstrates') is unsupported by limited testing. Finding 10 identifies similar overstatement in the conclusion about universal superiority across all tasks/modalities/scales.
GT identifies selective omission of actual FID values (using '✗' instead) and ambiguity in ΔFLOPs reporting in Table 4. No finding addresses these specific data integrity issues in the table.

Both identify fabricated relevance of the plant grafting citation. GT notes reference [4] is misattributed as inspiring the computational method. Finding 7 identifies the same issue: the plant biology paper is falsely claimed to discuss neural network activation transfer.

Both identify contradictory claims about locality metric L_k at k=32. GT notes the interpretation problem with averaging. Finding 8 identifies direct contradiction between text claiming 'all 28 layers exhibit L_k > 0.7' vs. figure caption stating '15 out of 28 layers exceed 0.5.'

Both identify experimental design issues with PixArt-Σ evaluation. GT questions whether baseline used same sampling steps and whether LoRA vs. full finetuning affects comparison. Finding 9 identifies data leakage: synthetic training data uses prompts from the evaluation set.

GT identifies misleading comparison in Table 6 where grafted model (712M params) is compared to TinyDiT-D14 (340M params) without acknowledging the parameter count difference. No finding addresses this specific unfair comparison issue.

GT identifies omission of limitations and failure cases from the conclusion (100% replacement failures, PixArt artifacts, bias risks). While finding 10 notes overstated claims, it doesn't specifically address the ethical omission of known limitations.

GT identifies selective reporting of speedup at non-standard batch size=2 in Table 5. Findings 3 and 4 both identify inconsistency in the reported 1.43× speedup claim, with actual table data showing 1.59× speedup, addressing the same data integrity issue.

GT identifies incoherence between abstract's '<2% compute' claim and the actual data percentage (10% vs. 20%) used for best results shown in Figure 4(a). No finding addresses this specific cross-section inconsistency about training data percentage.

GT identifies inappropriate promotional language ('revolutionary,' 'paradigm shift,' 'unprecedented') in the introduction. While finding 6 mentions 'paradigm shift' in Section 6, it focuses on the unsupported claim rather than the rhetorical manipulation itself.

GT identifies incorrect FLOP calculation formula in Section H.1 and inconsistency with reported ΔFLOPs_op reductions. No finding addresses this specific methodological error in computational complexity analysis.

GT identifies misrepresentation of reference [52] in Appendix A related work, which focuses on few-shot learning rather than architectural editing. No finding addresses this specific citation misrepresentation in the related work section.
